answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the yarrow check immediately, the inlet audit keeps the resolved set and the ridge replay publishes exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 149 aliases therefore pays the reading cost 149 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 30 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
